draft.change: Clarify the existing Gen.4.7 citation under is-it-not by showing the scope of the opening particle.
draft.definition: With interrogative הֲ־, לֹא frames a question to which the speaker expects an affirmative answer.
draft.evidence: In Gen.4.7 the initial הֲלוֹא asks Cain to affirm the consequence of אִם תֵּיטִיב, “if you do well.”

analysis.evidence: הֲלוֹא opens the whole question אִם תֵּיטִיב שְׂאֵת, asking Cain to acknowledge that doing well brings lifting up. The condition itself is positive. The contrasting condition וְאִם לֹא תֵיטִיב places לֹא directly before the verb to say “if you do not do well.”
analysis.morphology: Interrogative prefix הֲ־ attached to the negative particle לֹא, here spelled לוֹא.
analysis.sense: Introduces a rhetorical question expecting agreement.

analysis.evidence: אִם תֵּיטִיב means “if you do well.” The parallel וְאִם לֹא תֵיטִיב, “and if you do not do well,” confirms that the marked אִם introduces the first of two contrasting conditions. הֲלוֹא marks the rhetorical question.
analysis.morphology: Conditional conjunction without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אִם תֵּיטִיב addresses Cain directly. The verb has no expressed object, and the contrasting clause וְאִם לֹא תֵיטִיב warns that sin crouches at the door. The contrast concerns how Cain acts.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperfect, second person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: שְׂאֵת gives the result of אִם תֵּיטִיב, “if you do well.” The preceding question asks why Cain’s face has fallen (Genesis 4:6). A “lifting” of his face answers that question and conveys acceptance.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וְאִם לֹא תֵיטִיב means “and if you do not do well.” לֹא negates תֵיטִיב within the condition, reversing the preceding אִם תֵּיטִיב, “if you do well.”
analysis.morphology: Negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וְאִם לֹא תֵיטִיב means “and if you do not do what is right.” It repeats the verb from אִם תֵּיטִיב in the preceding condition, now with לֹא, and introduces the warning to Cain that sin crouches at the door.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperfect, second person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: In לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ, the phrase לַפֶּתַח locates sin as it crouches. The doorway is the threshold in the image of sin lying in wait for Cain.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ with the definite article הַ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ depicts sin crouching at the doorway. Although חַטָּאת is grammatically feminine, the masculine participle רֹבֵץ presents it as a crouching creature. The following clauses describe its desire for Cain and call on him to master it.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: sin as a power that lies in wait, pursues, overthrows

analysis.evidence: לַפֶּתַח locates the action at the doorway. רֹבֵץ pictures sin as a creature crouching there. Although חַטָּאת ‘sin’ is grammatically feminine, the participle is masculine singular, as are the following suffixes in תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ ‘its desire’ and בּוֹ ‘over it’.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: lie down in a crouched posture

analysis.evidence: וְאֵלֶיךָ תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ means “and its desire is toward you.” וְאֵלֶיךָ identifies Cain as the one toward whom the desire is directed. The suffix ־וֹ refers back to the figure described as crouching at the door.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: The ending of תִּמְשָׁל already marks Cain as the person addressed. The explicit וְאַתָּה sets him in contrast to the preceding clause וְאֵלֶיךָ תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ, “its desire is for you.”
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to an independent second-person masculine singular pronoun.
analysis.sense: you, as for you (the one addressed set apart)

analysis.evidence: The explicit subject וְאַתָּה (and you) addresses Cain. The complement בּוֹ (over it) identifies what he is to rule over, the sin depicted as crouching at the door and desiring him.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine singular
